function.mechanism: Steviol glycosides activate sweet-taste signaling and deliver high sweetness intensity with minimal caloric contribution; commercial forms include leaf-derived and bioconverted glycosides.

adi.basis: Expressed as steviol equivalents; EFSA 2024 concluded evidence was insufficient to raise ADI above 4 mg/kg bw/day.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA 2026 found no safety concern for the modified E960c production process; EFSA 2024 retained the ADI at 4 mg/kg bw/day and flagged increased conservative exceedance risk in toddlers under proposed expanded uses.

notable_bans: U.S. restriction: whole-leaf and crude stevia extracts are not permitted for use as sweeteners (distinct from high-purity steviol glycosides).

concerns.summary: Conservative dietary exposure scenarios indicate possible ADI exceedance in high-consuming toddlers/young children in some modeled conditions.
Broader non-nutritive sweetener literature continues to evaluate gut-related mechanisms; a recent in vitro study reported no epithelial barrier disruption for stevia in tested conditions.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2026 concluded no safety concern for E960c process modification (including use of new GM production strains) under proposed specifications.
JECFA continues to list ADI 0-4 mg/kg bw (as steviol), with latest listed evaluation year 2023.
Recent review-level evidence did not identify consistent genotoxic or carcinogenic potential for steviol glycosides within nonsugar sweeteners.

populations: toddlers (95th percentile, conservative EU scenario under proposed expanded uses)
young children with high modeled intake
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2024 and JECFA historical exposure summaries both indicate that high-end child intake can approach or exceed the ADI in conservative models.

risk_assessment.rationale: Steviol glycosides are broadly approved and repeatedly judged acceptable under current specifications, but finite ADI and modeled exceedance risk in high-consuming children prevent a lower-risk tier.
key_factors: EFSA retained ADI at 4 mg/kg bw/day rather than increasing it
Modeled toddler/young-child exceedance risk in conservative scenarios
No IARC listing found for steviol glycosides
FDA GRAS no-questions responses for multiple high-purity steviol glycoside preparations
